_comment: edit-lesson replies (Edit with AI on one lesson's row, #1242): one request, no plan. The key is a [fixture:NAME] token in the request (default: 'default'). The replies are text, so {{frozen}} can stand for the lesson's own id, slug, title, unit, group, level, order and prerequisites (as JSON members): 'default' fits any lesson of any course and rewrites its text, summary, vocabulary and questions. 'renames' gives the lesson a new id and slug, so the result check refuses it (asked again twice, then the run stops with the course unchanged). 'invalid-json' can't be read; 'slow' is 'default' after 3 s. See docs/testing.md.

default.reply:
{{{frozen}}, "summary": "Edited with AI: more worked examples", "content": "## The idea

This lesson was edited from your request: more worked examples, simpler words.

## Worked example

6/8 = 3/4, because both top and bottom divide by 2.

## Check

Multiply back to check your answer.", "vocabulary": [{"term": "numerator", "meaning": "the number on top of a fraction", "example": "In 3/4 the numerator is 3.", "example_meaning": "3 parts are taken"}], "quiz": [{"question_id": "{{slug}}-e01", "prompt": "Simplify 2/4 and give it as a decimal.", "type": "numeric", "correct_answer": "0.5", "explanation": "2/4 = 1/2 = 0.5", "hint": "Divide top and bottom by 2."}, {"question_id": "{{slug}}-e02", "prompt": "1/2 is bigger than 1/3.", "type": "true-false", "correct_answer": "true", "explanation": "Halves are bigger pieces than thirds."}]}
